error_rate_limited: Too many failed attempts. Please try again in {seconds} seconds.
error_job_name_exists: A job with this name already exists
error_credential_in_use: Credential is in use by one or more jobs
error_password_too_short: Password must be at least 8 characters
error_source_dirs_required: At least one source directory must be specified
error_password_same: New password must be different from current password
auth_sign_in_description: Sign in to manage your backups
auth_totp_description: Enter the 6-digit code from your authenticator app
setup_description: Let's set up your backup system. Create an admin account to get started.
setup_admin_note: This will be the only administrator account. You can change the password later in settings.
jobs_no_jobs_description: Get started by creating your first backup job.
jobs_no_matching_description: Try adjusting your filters to find what you're looking for.
job_status_enabled_desc: This job will run on schedule
job_destination_not_supported: This destination type is not yet supported.
job_sources_help: The folders on your system that you want to back up. You can add multiple directories, and each will be synced to a matching subfolder in the destination.
job_confirm_delete_message: Are you sure you want to delete "{name}"? This action cannot be undone.
job_confirm_mirror_message: Mirror Mode will delete files from the backup destination that no longer exist in the source. This can result in permanent data loss if files are accidentally deleted from the source. Are you sure you want to continue?
job_validation_source_required: At least one source directory must be selected
job_validation_credentials_required: Please select credentials for this provider
provider_local_description: Rsync to local or mounted drives
local_usb_drive_description: Select a USB drive to use for backups
local_usb_drive_help: Select a USB drive to automatically mount before backup. The drive is identified by its unique UUID, so it will work regardless of which USB port you use.
local_mount_point_description: Where the drive will be mounted
local_mount_point_help: The directory path where your backup destination will be accessible. For USB drives, this is where the drive gets mounted.
local_backup_subdir_description: Folder on the drive for backups
local_backup_subdir_help: A subfolder within the mount point where backups will be stored.
local_auto_mount_help: Automatically mount the selected USB drive before the backup starts.
local_auto_mount_desc: Mount the USB drive automatically when the job runs.
local_auto_unmount_help: Safely unmount the USB drive after backup completes.
local_auto_unmount_desc: Safely unmount the drive when the backup completes.
local_preview: Files will be backed up to: {path}
s3_bucket_description: The name of your S3 bucket where backups will be stored.
s3_bucket_help: The name of your S3 bucket where backups will be stored.
s3_region_description: The AWS region where your bucket is located.
s3_region_help: The AWS region where your bucket is located. Select 'Custom Endpoint' for S3-compatible services like MinIO or Backblaze B2.
s3_custom_endpoint_description: For S3-compatible services like MinIO or Backblaze B2.
s3_custom_endpoint_help: The URL for S3-compatible services like MinIO, Backblaze B2, or Wasabi.
s3_custom_endpoint_note: For MinIO, Backblaze B2, Wasabi, or other S3-compatible services.
s3_path_prefix_description: Optional folder path within the bucket.
s3_path_prefix_help: A prefix (folder path) within the bucket where backups will be stored.
s3_storage_class_description: Choose based on access frequency and cost requirements.
s3_storage_class_help: The S3 storage class to use. Different classes have different pricing and retrieval times.
s3_preview: Files will be stored at: s3://{bucket}/{prefix}
sftp_host_help: The hostname or IP address of the SSH/SFTP server.
sftp_username_help: The SSH username to authenticate with.
sftp_remote_path_description: Directory on the remote server for backups.
sftp_remote_path_help: The directory path on the remote server where backups will be stored.
sftp_key_auth_help: Authenticate using an SSH key pair. First, add your PUBLIC key to ~/.ssh/authorized_keys on the server, then store your PRIVATE key in the credentials here. More secure than passwords.
webdav_url_help: The WebDAV endpoint URL. For Nextcloud, this is usually https://your-server.com/remote.php/dav/files/username/
webdav_remote_path_description: Directory on the server for backups.
webdav_remote_path_help: The folder path within your WebDAV server where backups will be stored.
google_drive_folder_id_description: The ID of the Google Drive folder for backups. Leave empty for root.
google_drive_folder_id_help: The ID of the Google Drive folder where backups will be stored. Leave empty to use the root of your Drive. You can find the folder ID in the URL when viewing the folder in Google Drive.
google_drive_shared_drive_help: Leave empty to use your personal 'My Drive'. Specify a Shared Drive ID to sync to a team drive.
google_drive_preview_folder: Files will be synced to folder: {id}
google_drive_preview_root: Files will be synced to root of your Google Drive
google_drive_setup_desc: Google Drive uses OAuth authentication. You'll need to:
google_drive_setup_step1: Create a project in the Google Cloud Console
google_drive_setup_step4: Complete the OAuth flow to obtain access and refresh tokens
onedrive_folder_path_help: The folder path in your OneDrive where backups will be stored. Use forward slashes, e.g., /Backups/MyServer
onedrive_drive_id_description: Optional. For SharePoint or shared drives.
onedrive_drive_id_help: Leave empty to use your personal OneDrive. Specify a drive ID to use a shared drive or SharePoint document library.
onedrive_preview: Files will be synced to: OneDrive{path}
onedrive_setup_desc: OneDrive uses OAuth authentication. You'll need to add your Microsoft account credentials using the "Add Credentials" button above. The credentials will be securely stored and used to access your OneDrive.
credentials_ssh_setup_info: Add your public key to {path} on the server, then paste your private key below.
credentials_refresh_token_help: The refresh token is used to automatically renew access tokens when they expire.
credentials_oauth_onedrive_help: To get OAuth tokens, you'll need to register an app in the Azure Portal and complete the OAuth flow to obtain access and refresh tokens.
credentials_oauth_google_help: To get OAuth tokens, you'll need to set up OAuth credentials in the Google Cloud Console and complete the OAuth flow.
credentials_error_s3_incomplete: Please fill in all S3 credential fields
credentials_error_ssh_key_required: Please provide an SSH private key
credentials_error_webdav_incomplete: Please fill in all WebDAV credential fields
credentials_error_oauth_incomplete: Please fill in all OAuth credential fields
sync_mirror_mode_description: Creates an exact mirror of the source. If you delete a file from your source, it will also be deleted from the backup on the next run.
sync_exclude_patterns_description: Files and folders matching these patterns will not be backed up.
sync_dry_run_description: Simulate the backup without making changes. Useful for testing.
sync_checksum_description: Use checksums instead of timestamps to detect changes. More accurate but slower.
sync_compress_description: Compress data during transfer. Reduces bandwidth but uses more CPU.
sync_bandwidth_limit_description: Limit transfer speed in KB/s. Leave empty for unlimited.
sync_verbosity_description: Amount of detail in backup logs.
schedule_cron_description: Standard cron format: minute hour day month weekday
history_no_runs_description: Runs will appear here after your first backup.
history_confirm_delete: Are you sure you want to delete this run? The log data will be permanently removed.
settings_show_log_viewer: Show log viewer after manual runs
settings_show_log_viewer_desc: Automatically open the log viewer dialog when you manually start a backup job.
settings_auto_show_last_page_desc: Automatically scroll to show new log entries as they arrive.
settings_refresh_interval_desc: How often to refresh and show the latest page.
settings_2fa_description: Add an extra layer of security to your account.
settings_2fa_low_codes: Low recovery codes. Consider re-enabling 2FA for new codes.
settings_2fa_disable_description: Enter your password and current authenticator code to disable 2FA.
settings_retention_invalid: Please enter a valid number (minimum 1) or leave empty for unlimited
settings_retention_description: Control how many job runs are kept in history.
settings_retention_help: When set, older runs are automatically deleted when new runs exceed the limit.
totp_setup_step1_desc: Download Google Authenticator, Authy, or similar app on your phone.
totp_setup_step2_desc: Scan this QR code with your authenticator app.
totp_setup_manual_entry: Can't scan? Enter this code manually:
totp_setup_step3_desc: Enter the 6-digit code from your authenticator app to verify setup.
totp_setup_step4_desc: Store these codes safely. Each can be used once if you lose access to your authenticator.
path_selector_tip: Tip: You can also type a path directly in the input field.
path_selector_error_not_accessible: "{path}" is not accessible. Select an allowed path below.
history_no_matching_description: Try adjusting your filters to find what you're looking for.
history_purge_all_confirm: Are you sure you want to delete all backup history? This action cannot be undone.
history_purge_job_confirm: Are you sure you want to delete all history for "{name}"? This action cannot be undone.
history_purge_run_confirm: Are you sure you want to delete this run? This action cannot be undone.
schedule_help: Set up automatic backup times. You can add multiple schedules. Without a schedule, backups only run when you click 'Run Now'.
schedule_no_schedules: No schedules configured. Backups will only run manually.
schedule_days_help: Select one or more days. The backup will run at the specified time on each selected day.
schedule_interval_help: Set how often the backup should run. Note: Very frequent backups may impact system performance.
schedule_cron_help: Advanced scheduling using cron syntax. Five fields: minute, hour, day of month, month, day of week.
schedule_cron_format: Format: minute hour day-of-month month day-of-week
schedule_pending: Will be created when job is saved
sync_mirror_desc: Delete files from destination that no longer exist in source.
sync_checksum_desc: Compare files by checksum instead of modification time and size. Slower but more accurate.
sync_checksum_help: Compare files by checksum instead of modification time and size. Slower but catches every change.
sync_checksum_disabled_by_force: Disabled when Force Sync is active (all files transfer anyway).
sync_compression_desc: Compress data during transfer. Useful for slow connections, but adds CPU overhead.
sync_compression_help: Compress data during transfer. Useful for slow network connections, but adds CPU overhead.
sync_ignore_times_desc: Always transfer files regardless of modification time. Ideal for encrypted containers like VeraCrypt.
sync_ignore_times_help: Ignores file timestamps when deciding what to transfer. Use this for files that change internally without updating their modification time, such as encrypted containers.
sync_dry_run_desc: Show what would be transferred without actually doing it. Good for testing.
sync_dry_run_help: Simulates the backup without actually copying any files. Perfect for testing a new job configuration.
sync_verbosity_help: Controls how much information is output during backup. Quiet mode only shows errors.
sync_verbosity_quiet_desc: Only errors will be shown in the logs.
sync_verbosity_normal_desc: Shows which files are transferred and summary statistics.
sync_verbosity_verbose_desc: Shows per-file progress bars, speeds, and detailed statistics.
sync_bandwidth_help: Limits how fast data is transferred. Useful if backing up over a network.
sync_exclude_help: Files and folders matching these patterns will be skipped. Use wildcards like *.tmp or specific folder names.
totp_enable_desc: Use an authenticator app like Google Authenticator or Aegis.
totp_scan_instruction: Scan with your authenticator app, then enter the code below.
totp_save_codes_desc: Use them to sign in if you lose access to your authenticator.
totp_protected_message: Your account is now protected with two-factor authentication.
